units.text: For some say, at Dracanum; and some, on windy Icarus;
and some, in Naxos, O Heaven-born, Insewn; and others
by the deep-eddying river Alpheus that pregnant Semele
bare you to Zeus the thunder-lover.
And others yet, lord, say you were born in Thebes; but all
these lie. The Father of men and gods gave you birth remote from men
and secretly from white-armed Hera. There is a
certain Nysa, a mountain most high and richly grown with woods, far
off in Phoenice, near the streams of Aegyptus
“and men will lay up for her many offerings in her
shrines. And as these things are three, so shall mortals ever sacrifice perfect hecatombs
to you at your feasts each three
years.”The Son of Cronos spoke and nodded with his dark brows.
And the divine locks of the king flowed forward
from his immortal head, and he made great Olympus reel. So
spake wise Zeus and ordained it with a nod. Be
favorable, O Insewn, Inspirer of frenzied women! we singers sing of
you as we begin and as we end a strain, and none
forgetting you may call holy song to mind.
And so, farewell, Dionysus, Insewn, with
your mother Semele whom men call Thyone.
